abstract.para: This dataset provides the results for quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) of peat samples collected from ambient and experimental plots in the Spruce and Peatland Responses Under Climatic and Environmental Change (SPRUCE) experiment site in June and August of 2021, and June of 2022. SPRUCE is located within the Marcell Experimental Forest in northern Minnesota, USA. The dataset includes bacterial, archaeal, fungal gene copy numbers, along with corresponding logarithmic values, at 11 depth increments of two-meter deep peat cores taken from 12 sampling sites locations inside SPRUCE plots (10 chambered and 2 ambient plots). The sampling, sample prep and analysis followed standard methods outlined in prior publications (Wilson et al. 2016; Kluber et al. 2020) except that a higher yielding Omega Bio-Tek Mag-Bind Environmental DNA 96 Kit was used for extractions and DNA was quantified using Qubit dsDNA High Sensitivity Assay Kit. qPCR subsamples of peat cores from the SPRUCE plots characterize changes in the abundance and composition of microbial communities of peat seasonally showing how composition varies under multiple levels of experimental peat warming and atmospheric CO2 concentrations.

This dataset contains one data file in comma-separated values (.csv) format. Additional metadata are provided: one data dictionary and a file-level metadata file in comma-separated values (.csv) format and a user guide in PDF (*.pdf) format.

On 2026-07-07 this dataset was updated to add three columns to the data file: ‘Fungal_copy_dry’, ‘Log_fungal_copy_dry’, ‘Fungal_copy_wet’. No previously released data values were altered. Additionally, the abstract, data dictionary, and user guide were updated, and a file-level metadata file was added.

description.para: Observations occurred at The Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s SPRUCE (Spruce and Peatland Responses Under Changing Environments) project (Hanson et al., 2017) at S1 bog at the U.S. Forest Service’s Marcell Experimental Forest, in Minnesota, USA (47.51, -93.45). SPRUCE is an ecosystem-scale study that warms the vegetation and peatland soil profile to a depth of 2 m within 12.8-m diameter open-top enclosures. The peat was heated first at – 2 m for a period of 1 year starting in summer 2014 (deep peat heating phase), then heating of the overlying air began in August 2015 starting the whole ecosystem warming phase of the experiment.

Cores were extracted from hollows in each of the 10 experimental plots (4, 6, 8, 10, 11,13, 16, 17, 19, and 20) and two ambient plots (7 and 21) on 3 dates (2021-06-23, 2021-08-24, 2022-06-21). On each sampling date, cores extending to 200 cm below the hollow surface were collected using a knife to cut out low density surface peat to a depth of approximately 30cm, and below that using a Russian corer. Peat is then divided into 10 cm intervals from 0 and 50 cm and 25 cm intervals below 50 cm depth. Sub-samples were then frozen on dry ice in the field and shipped to ORNL where they were stored at -80°C or -20°C prior to processing. The 125-150 cm and 175-200 cm increments were excluded from qPCR analyses.

A subsample of ~0.25g of field-wet peat was taken from peat collected from each of the previously described plots and depths, and DNA was extracted using the Omega Bio-Tek Mag-Bind Environmental DNA 96 Kit (Omega Bio-Tek) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. DNA was eluted in 100 µL of Elution Buffer (Omega Bio-Tek). DNA extracts were further processed through the DNA Clean and Concentrator Kit-25 (Zymo Research) according to the manufacturer’s protocol to remove contaminants and to concentrate the DNA in a final volume of 50 µL. The concentration of extracted DNA for each sample was quantified using the Qubit dsDNA HS Assay Kit (ThermoFisher Scientific).

The same general approach outlined by Kluber et al. (2020) was then used to quantify gene copy number g-1 dry soil for bacteria, fungi, and archaea. Analyses were set up in clear 96-well plates. Each qPCR reaction consisted of 18µl of MasterMix—6 µl H2O, 1µl of forward primer (at 10 µM), 1µl of reverse primer (at 10 µM), and 10µl of SYBR Green SuperMix (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc.)—combined with 2µl of a 1:10 dilution of DNA from each SPRUCE sample or known standard. Three technical replicates were conducted for each sample and standard. The primers used to quantify bacterial, archaeal, and fungal gene abundance are described in Table 1:
Table 1: DNA primer sequences used to quantify bacterial, fungal, and archaeal gene copy number.
Bacterial F - EUB338 | ACT CCT ACG GGA GGC AGC AG | Lane, 1991
Bacterial R - EUB518 | ATT ACC GCG GCT GCT GG | Muyzer et al., 1993
Fungal F - nu-SSU-1196F | GGA AAC TCA CCA GGT CCA GA | Borneman & Hartin, 2000
Fungal R - nu-SSU-1536R | ATT GCA ATG CYC TAT CCC CA | Borneman & Hartin, 2000
Archaeal F - rRNA 915F | AGG AAT TGG CGG GGG AGC AC | Colwell et al., 2008
Archaeal R - rRNA 1059R | GCC ATG CAC CWCCTC T | Yu et al., 2005

Genomic DNA from Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 (bacteria), Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C (fungi), and Methanococcus maripaludis C5 (archaea) was used to create a standard linear curve for each microbial Kingdom of interest. DNA from qPCR standards was diluted to 1:10, 1:100, 1:1,000, and 1:10,000 and used to generate a standard linear curve relating the log of the gene copy number to the measured threshold value (Ct). The standard curve was used to calculate gene copy number g-1 dry soil in SPRUCE samples based on sample Ct values measured by the CFX96 Real-Time System (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc.). Gene copy numbers of technical replicates were averaged (mean).
